Calculation_Methodology: Direct measurement: equipment fuel consumption logged daily. Blasting explosives: 500 tons/yr × 0.18 kg CO2e/kg TNT equivalent
Notes: Scope 1: All direct mining operations. Equipment: excavators (350 tons/yr fuel), compressors (150 tons), vehicles (300 tons). Blasting: 500 tons explosive material.

Calculation_Methodology: Location-based: 90,000 MWh purchased × 0.5 kg CO2/kWh grid average
Notes: Scope 2 Location-based: Poland average grid ~0.5 kg CO2e/kWh (coal-heavy). Market-based (renewable purchases): 10% of electricity = 81,000 tCO2e location vs 67,500 market.

Calculation_Methodology: Market-based: (90,000 MWh × 90% grid) × 0.5 + (9,000 MWh × 0.05 kg CO2/kWh renewable)
Emission_Factor_Source: EU renewable factor 0.05 kg/kWh, grid 0.5 kg/kWh
Notes: Scope 2 Market-based: Accounts for 10% renewable energy certificates purchased.

Calculation_Methodology: Financed emissions: 1.5M tons coal produced × 0.453 kg CO2e/kg coal (IPCC combustion factor)
Emission_Factor_Source: IPCC AR6 combustion factors for thermal coal
Notes: Scope 3: Coal combustion at end-customer power plants. 1.5M tons coal × 0.453 = 680,000 tCO2e. Assumption: 95% burned, 5% stockpiled/waste.

Calculation_Methodology: Direct measurement: gas flaring volume logged daily at wellheads. 150 MMcf/yr flared × 0.0557 kg CO2e per cubic meter
Emission_Factor_Source: EPA flaring emission factors, operator field data
Notes: Scope 1: Flaring at 12 production sites. Winter flaring 60% of total (high pressure/safety). Summer flaring 40%. Fugitive emissions (leaks) add ~10,000 tCO2e.

Calculation_Methodology: Location-based: 250,000 MWh × 0.38 kg CO2/kWh (Norway grid, 95% hydro)
Notes: Scope 2: Offshore platform electricity from mainland grid. Norwegian grid is one of cleanest in Europe (0.38 kg CO2/kWh average).

Calculation_Methodology: Use-phase emissions: 5M barrels oil × 410 kg CO2/barrel + 20 BCF gas × 0.0567 kg CO2e/cubic meter
Notes: Scope 3: End-customer combustion of oil/gas products. 5M barrels × 410 kg/barrel (accounting for refining losses) + gas combustion.

Calculation_Methodology: No direct emissions from solar generation. Grid balancing by grid operator.
Notes: Scope 1: Zero direct emissions from solar PV generation operations.

Calculation_Methodology: Minimal: Inverter controls, security systems: 1,200 MWh × 0.42 kg CO2/kWh (Spain grid)
Notes: Scope 2: Small parasitic loads for inverters, monitoring systems, grid balancing.

Calculation_Methodology: Embodied emissions: 80 MWp capacity × 30-40 kg CO2e per MWp (panel manufacturing upstream)
Notes: Scope 3: Lifecycle embodied emissions in solar panel manufacturing. Aluminum frames, silicon refining, glass production. Allocated across 25-year lifetime = ~100 tCO2e/year.

Calculation_Methodology: No direct emissions from wind generation.
Notes: Scope 1: Zero direct emissions from onshore wind turbine operation.

Calculation_Methodology: Minimal: Control systems, heating: 500 MWh × 0.4 kg CO2/kWh (Germany grid)
Notes: Scope 2: Small loads for control systems, heated tower base in winter.

Calculation_Methodology: Embodied: 120 MW capacity × 15 kg CO2e per MW (turbine steel, rare earths)
Notes: Scope 3: Turbine manufacturing (steel, REE magnets), concrete foundation, shipping. Allocated over 25-year lifetime = ~72 tCO2e/year.

Calculation_Methodology: Natural gas combustion: 4.5M cubic meters × 2.04 kg CO2e per cubic meter (gas combustion factor)
Notes: Scope 1: Natural gas for heating/hot water across 35 properties. Winter peak: 8M m3, summer: 1M m3. Office buildings 60%, retail 40%.

Calculation_Methodology: Location-based: 145,000 MWh × 0.4 kg CO2/kWh (Germany grid average 2023)
Notes: Scope 2: Electricity for HVAC, lighting, elevators. Location-based accounts for average German grid. Market-based (renewable contracts): would be 20% lower.

Calculation_Methodology: Waste management & water: 3,500 tons waste × 0.3 kg CO2/kg (transport + landfill) + 2.5M m3 water × 0.003 kg CO2/m3 treatment
Emission_Factor_Source: EPA waste factors, local water authority
Notes: Scope 3: Waste hauling (85%), landfill (treatment), water treatment. Excludes embodied carbon in building construction (would be allocated per year = 500+ tCO2e).

Calculation_Methodology: Natural gas: 8.5M cubic meters × 2.04 kg CO2e/m3 (residential heating factor)
Emission_Factor_Source: IPCC combustion, meter readings from residents
Notes: Scope 1: Heating across 450 residential units. Highly variable: cold winters increase 30%, mild winters decrease 20%.

Calculation_Methodology: Location-based: 200,000 MWh × 0.36 kg CO2/kWh (Berlin grid)
Notes: Scope 2: Common area lighting, elevators, heating systems. 45% tenant-controlled, 55% building common.

Calculation_Methodology: Estimated from waste/water: 8M m3 water × 0.003 kg CO2/m3 + 4,000 tons waste × 0.3 kg/kg
Notes: Scope 3: Water supply and waste treatment. Does NOT include tenant energy use (counted as tenant scope 1/2).

Calculation_Methodology: Fuel consumption: 150,000 liters diesel machinery × 2.68 kg CO2e/liter + fertilizer application 500 tons × 0.5 kg CO2e/kg (N2O from nitrogen fertilizer)
Emission_Factor_Source: IPCC agriculture emission factors, fuel records
Notes: Scope 1: Machinery fuel (tractors 80%, irrigation pumps 20%) + fertilizer-induced N2O (high uncertainty +/-20%).

Calculation_Methodology: Fertilizer production & processing: 500 tons urea × 90 kg CO2e/kg (Haber-Bosch process) = 45,000 tCO2e. Crop processing (threshing, storage) = ~3,000 tCO2e.
Notes: Scope 3: Upstream fertilizer manufacturing (dominant cost). Haber-Bosch process for ammonia is extremely carbon-intensive. High uncertainty: +/- 30%.

Calculation_Methodology: Coal fuel input: 450,000 tons coal × 1.29 kg CO2e/kg (combustion + oxidation)
Emission_Factor_Source: IPCC coal combustion factors, fuel receipts
Notes: Scope 1: Direct coal combustion for electricity generation. Plant efficiency 38% (typical for coal). Coal quality: sub-bituminous (2.0 MJ/kg). Scrubber removes SO2/NOx but not CO2.

Calculation_Methodology: Plant auxiliary load: 150,000 MWh × 0.53 kg CO2/kWh (German grid). Pumps, fans, controls consume 3-5% of plant electricity.
Notes: Scope 2: Parasitic plant loads (coal pulverizers, cooling pump drives, controls). Backup purchase from grid.

Calculation_Methodology: Iron ore reduction: 180,000 tons ore × 0.69 kg CO2e/kg iron (from coke combustion + oxidation)
Notes: Scope 1: Blast furnace direct reduction (80% of emissions). Electricity (from coal grid) adds another 50,000 tCO2e if counted here (usually allocated to Scope 2).

Calculation_Methodology: Electricity for operations: 200,000 MWh × 0.34 kg CO2/kWh (German grid, renewable mix increasing)
Notes: Scope 2: Smelting furnaces, casting, rolling mills powered by grid (coal+renewables 40% + hydro 30% + nuclear 10% = 0.34 kg/kWh average).

Calculation_Methodology: Fleet maintenance: 8,000 liters diesel fuel × 2.68 kg CO2e/liter + gasoline 1,500 liters × 2.31 kg CO2e/liter
Notes: Scope 1: Maintenance vehicle fleet for road repairs, drainage cleaning, bridge inspection. Heavy equipment (excavators, graders) during maintenance windows.

Calculation_Methodology: Downstream user emissions: Not counted by infrastructure owner, but disclosure-relevant. 500M vehicle-km × 0.9 kg CO2e/km average (EU fleet mix).
Notes: Scope 3 (informational): End-user emissions from vehicles using the road network. Not typically counted as infrastructure owner scope 3 (boundary issue). Included for full transparency.

Calculation_Methodology: Chemical synthesis: Ammonia production (Haber-Bosch) 500 tons × 50 kg CO2e/kg = 25,000 tCO2e. Other syntheses (organics) = 10,000 tCO2e. Oxidation fugitive emissions 2,500 tCO2e.
Emission_Factor_Source: IPCC process emission factors for chemical manufacturing
Notes: Scope 1: Process emissions from chemical synthesis reactions (not combustion). Highly process-dependent.

Calculation_Methodology: Electricity: 180,000 MWh × 0.27 kg CO2/kWh. Steam: 50,000 tons steam × 0.16 kg CO2e/kg (on-site boiler, natural gas).
Notes: Scope 2: Electricity (Belgium has low-carbon grid from nuclear), steam from on-site gas boiler. Belgium grid = 0.27 kg CO2/kWh (much lower than EU average 0.4).

Calculation_Methodology: Natural gas for heating/cooking: 8M m3 × 1.89 kg CO2e/m3 (food processing uses more gas than office) + refrigeration fugitive emissions: 3,000 tCO2e (HFC/HFO leaks, 50 tons × 60 kg CO2e/kg GWP)
Emission_Factor_Source: IPCC gas combustion + refrigerant GWP factors
Notes: Scope 1: Facility heating for processing (pasteurization, sterilization) + refrigeration system leaks (packaging chilling systems lose ~5% charge/year).

Calculation_Methodology: Process electricity: 50,000 MWh × 0.36 kg CO2/kWh (Netherlands grid, increasing renewables)
Notes: Scope 2: Processing machinery (sorting, conveyor, mixing, packaging), water treatment, wastewater treatment.

Calculation_Methodology: Agricultural input emissions: Grains 2,000 tons × 0.3 kg CO2e/kg (embodied from farming) = 600 tCO2e. Fruits 1,500 tons × 0.25 = 375. Sugar 500 tons × 0.35 = 175. Total agricultural = 1,150 tCO2e. Transport upstream (farms to factory): 500 km × 0.12 kg CO2e/ton/km × 5,000 tons = 300 tCO2e. Transport downstream (factory to distribution): 1,000 km × 0.08 kg/ton/km × 5,000 tons = 400 tCO2e.
Emission_Factor_Source: IPCC agricultural production factors, food transport factors
Notes: Scope 3: High uncertainty in agricultural emissions (farm practices vary wildly). Supply chain transport (upstream + downstream). Assumes 30% transport loss/spoilage.

Calculation_Methodology: Diesel fuel consumption: 3,500 tons bunker fuel × 3.15 kg CO2e/kg (marine diesel combustion, slightly higher energy density than road diesel)
Notes: Scope 1: Fishing vessel fuel (trawlers 70%, longiners 20%, nets 10%). Fuel consumption peaks in winter (rough seas = higher RPM).

Calculation_Methodology: Fish processing/freezing: 800 tons catch × 15 kg CO2e/kg (frozen storage energy + transport) = 12,000 tCO2e. Packaging/distribution: 8M kg × 0.001 kg CO2e/kg = 8,000 tCO2e. Total = ~18,000 tCO2e.
Emission_Factor_Source: Food processing emission factors, packaging emissions
Notes: Scope 3: Post-harvest processing (icing, freezing, storage) is energy-intensive. Includes supply chain to market.

Calculation_Methodology: Electricity for pumping + chemical treatment: 45,000 MWh electricity × 0.2 kg CO2/kWh (facility renewable mix) + chemicals (aluminum sulfate, chlorine): 500 tons × 0.1 kg CO2e/kg = 50 tCO2e. Total ~9,000 + 50 = 9,050 tCO2e. Add backup generator fuel (rarely used): 2,950 tCO2e.
Emission_Factor_Source: IPCC treatment chemical factors, utility grid mix (often renewable-heavy)
Notes: Scope 1/2 hybrid: Pumping and chemical treatment. Utility often has renewable mix (hydro, solar) from own generation or contracts. Diesel backup rarely used (emergency only).

Calculation_Methodology: Pumping stations + office: 30,000 MWh × 0.27 kg CO2/kWh (Spain grid, 2023 includes 40% renewables)
Emission_Factor_Source: Spanish grid 2023 mix (solar + wind 40%, hydro 20%, thermal 40%)
Notes: Scope 2: Facility electricity (Spain has increasingly renewable grid). Pumping may be partially self-generated (hydro).

Calculation_Methodology: Chemical production upstream: Aluminum sulfate (alum) 2,000 tons × 2 kg CO2e/kg manufacturing = 4,000 tCO2e. Chlorine 200 tons × 2 kg CO2e/kg = 400 tCO2e. Lime 1,000 tons × 0.15 kg CO2e/kg = 150 tCO2e. Total = ~4,550 tCO2e (rounded to 6,000 with transport).
Notes: Scope 3: Upstream emissions of treatment chemicals (mining, synthesis, transport).

Calculation_Methodology: Heating fuel (propane backup, rarely used): 2,000 liters propane × 3.01 kg CO2e/liter = 6,020 tCO2e. Diesel for snow grooming: 1,500 liters × 2.68 = 4,020 tCO2e. Total = ~10,000 tCO2e (rounded from meter data = 8,000 actual).
Emission_Factor_Source: IPCC propane/diesel combustion factors, fuel receipts
Notes: Scope 1: Heating fuel (propane, rarely used in season due to electric heating). Snow grooming fuel (winter operations). Minimal in spring/summer/fall.

Calculation_Methodology: Hotels + ski lifts + facilities: 60,000 MWh × 0.3 kg CO2/kWh (Swiss grid, nuclear + hydro heavy = 0.3 kg/kWh)
Emission_Factor_Source: Swiss grid 2023 mix (nuclear 35%, hydro 60%, thermal 5%) = low-carbon
Notes: Scope 2: Ski lifts (high power consumption during season), hotel common areas, restaurants, administration. Switzerland has one of cleanest grids in Europe.

Calculation_Methodology: Guest transport (downstream user emissions): 500,000 guest days × 50 km average drive to resort × 0.12 kg CO2e/km per car (occupancy 2.5 guests) = 1.2M guest-km × 0.12 = 144,000 tCO2e (downstream user impact). Supply chain (food delivery, supplies): 10,000 tons annual supply × 100 km avg distance × 0.05 kg CO2e/ton/km = 50,000 tCO2e upstream. Total = ~194,000 tCO2e (but typically only supply chain 12,000 counted as operator Scope 3).
Emission_Factor_Source: Transport emission factors, guest survey average distance data
Notes: Scope 3: Guest transport (informational only - not operator responsibility). Supply chain includes food + lodging supplies delivered to resort.
